title: Social Influence and the Allocation of Scientific Attention in AI Populations
abstract: arXiv:2609.22408v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI systems are becoming participants in the evaluation and use of scientific research. They encounter citation counts, download statistics and lists of popular articles developed around human readers, but the collective consequences of these signals for artificial readers remain uncertain. This paper adapts the Music Lab design to a market for academic attention. In the first experiment, 1,000 AI agents choose papers from the titles and abstracts of all 114 regular research articles published in the American Economic Review in 2025. The experiment has five independent-choice communities and five social-influence communities, each with 100 sequential agents. Only agents in the social-influence condition observe earlier selections within their community. Agents may select any number of papers. Social-information communities select 17.2 percent fewer papers per agent, concentrate their choices more heavily, and collectively cover 73 paper

translated_title: 社会影响与AI群体中科学注意力的分配
translated_abstract: AI系统正在成为科学研究的评估与使用中的参与者。它们会接触到引用次数、下载统计以及围绕人类读者建立的受欢迎文章列表，但这些信号对人工读者所产生的集体后果仍不确定。本文将“音乐实验室”实验设计应用于学术注意力市场。在第一个实验中，1,000个AI代理从2025年《美国经济评论》发表的全部114篇常规研究文章的标题和摘要中选择论文。实验设置了五个独立选择社区和五个社会影响社区，每个社区包含100个按顺序行动的代理。只有处于社会影响条件下的代理能够观察到其社区内其他代理较早的选择。代理可以选择任意数量的论文。结果显示，拥有社会信息的社区中每个代理选择的论文数量减少了17.2%，其选择更加集中，且集体覆盖范围仅限于73篇论文（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文将“音乐实验室”实验范式应用于学术注意力市场，通过1,000个AI代理的选择实验发现，社会影响会使AI代理的选择更加集中、覆盖的论文更少，揭示了社会信号对AI注意力分配的趋同和加剧不平等的效应。
en_tdlr: Adapting the Music Lab paradigm to a market for academic attention with 1,000 AI agents, this paper finds that social influence causes AI agents to concentrate their choices and cover fewer papers, revealing how social signals homogenize and skew the allocation of scientific attention in AI populations.
